impact:
Review round 12 produced ~22 findings that are ALL individually correct and all one class: a builtin replaced after this module loads defeats a decision the store makes, and nothing downstream re-derives it. Each was reproduced. Examples: `Number.isSafeInteger = () => true` makes `compareSourceVersions({a:20,b:NaN},{a:5,b:9})` answer "dominates", so a snapshot that REGRESSED a source publishes over a good one; `Object.keys = () => []` makes `canonicalSourceVersion({a:10})` persist `{}`; `RegExp.prototype.test = () => true` lets the id `../../../pwned` through the grammar so publish renames outside the store; `Hash.prototype.digest = () => "same"` collapses every checksum and every manifest identity, so an ABA manifest replacement reads as unchanged; `TextEncoder.prototype.encode = () => new Uint8Array()` commits empty artifacts while publish returns "published"; `fs.Stats.prototype.isFile = () => true` makes a FIFO read as a regular artifact.

WHY THIS IS FILED RATHER THAN FIXED IN T-010. The enumeration does not terminate, and that is demonstrable rather than a matter of opinion. `String.prototype.startsWith` is not on the reviewer's list; patching it makes `contained("/etc/passwd", root)` answer true and defeats containment outright (verified). After that come getters installed on `Object.prototype` for any key this code reads, `Symbol.toPrimitive` on any value it coerces, `Array.prototype[Symbol.iterator]`, `Function.prototype.bind`. Pinning names one at a time is the same treadmill rounds 9-11 were on — each fix removing one property read and introducing the next one further out — and a PARTIAL sweep is the worst outcome available, because it leaves the surface looking closed.

Closing it properly needs a hardened realm: every intrinsic frozen before any of this loads. That is a decision for the PROCESS, not for a library that ships into other people's — freezing `Object.prototype` from inside a dependency is hostile to consumers. It therefore belongs to the service (T-011), not to the store.

WHAT T-010 DID CLOSE, so the residual is not overstated: (1) the brand checks (WeakSet/WeakMap identity for the write authority and for file handles) are pinned, because those defend against a CALLER passing a forged authority or handle — an ordinary structural mistake, not a realm attacker, and a bounded one. (2) The prototype-POLLUTION class, which needs no attacker at all: `"value" in descriptor` consulting `Object.prototype.value`, and `this.name = ...` / `err.code = ...` invoking setters inherited from `Error.prototype`. Any dependency can cause those by accident, so all such sites now use pinned `hasOwn`/`defineOwn`, with two tests and two mutants.

THE DECISION NEEDED: does this product's threat model include arbitrary code running in the same realm as the snapshot store? If yes, the answer is realm hardening at process start (T-011), not per-name pinning, and this issue should be re-scoped to that. If no — and note that such code can call `fs.unlinkSync` on the store directly and skip every guard here — then `src/snapshot/intrinsics.ts` already records the correct scope and this issue closes as decided rather than as fixed.
title: Threat-model decision: in-realm intrinsic patching is not a boundary the snapshot store can defend
